speaker_role: student (QuestBridge applicant reviewing her own Yale admissions file)
key_insights: The interview functioned largely as a likability/'vibe check' rather than a technical evaluation; the interviewer explicitly scored based on warmth, thoughtfulness, and energy rather than credentials.

A weak interview did not sink her friend's application; the friend's interviewer wrote negative comments (no clear passions, seemed to be applying just for the name) and she was still admitted, suggesting interviews can help but rarely hurt.

Readers explicitly noted when her expressed passion (pre-med/neuroscience) didn't come through convincingly, and she later confirmed she wasn't truly interested in that field — genuine, articulable passion is something readers try to detect.

One reader's comment revealed that admissions officers sometimes compare recommendation letters from the same teacher across different applicants from the same high school within their assigned region.

The two readers gave meaningfully different overall assessments and comments about the same application, yet it still succeeded — illustrating real subjectivity/holistic tolerance in the process rather than a single hard bar.

She argues awards/accolades mattered less than having essays and recommendations that already conveyed the same character strengths, since her senior-year awards weren't included in her (September-submitted) application at all.
A missed administrative request (a second reader asked for an additional teacher recommendation, which she never saw/submitted) did not prevent admission.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Per a guest lecture by Yale's dean of admissions (as recounted by the speaker): about 50,000 total applications, roughly 2,000 admitted overall.
About 8,000-10,000 applications (roughly one-fifth) advance from individual readers to the committee pool.
The committee (5 people) meets 8am-5pm for five weeks reading applications; an application needs 4 of 5 committee votes to be admitted.
notable_or_distinctive: A rare direct look at real reader comments and numeric ratings, including the specific detail that a reader cross-referenced the same teacher's recommendation language across two different applicants from her school.
reliability_notes: Based on handwritten notes taken during a single file-review session (photos weren't allowed), so exact wording is the student's own transcription/paraphrase; the numeric rating scale (e.g., '2+', category scores) is not fully explained and may be misremembered; a single anecdotal case, not a description of general policy.
